---- MODULE W4Od6m8p6t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Banks, Motors, MaxRound, Nobody, InService

Isolation == [by : Banks, round : 0..MaxRound]

VARIABLES roomClaim, motorClaim, isolation, permitRound, standing

vars == <<roomClaim, motorClaim, isolation, permitRound, standing>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ roomClaim \in Banks \cup {Nobody}
    /\ motorClaim \in [Motors -> Banks \cup {Nobody}]
    /\ isolation \in [Motors -> Isolation \cup {InService}]
    /\ permitRound \in 0..MaxRound
    /\ standing \subseteq Banks

Init ==
    /\ roomClaim = Nobody
    /\ motorClaim = [m \in Motors |-> Nobody]
    /\ isolation = [m \in Motors |-> InService]
    /\ permitRound = 0
    /\ standing = Banks

TakeRoom(b) ==
    /\ b \in standing
    /\ roomClaim = Nobody
    /\ roomClaim' = b
    /\ UNCHANGED <<motorClaim, isolation, permitRound, standing>>

\* Coarse before fine: no motor claim without the machine-room claim.
TakeMotor(b, m) ==
    /\ roomClaim = b
    /\ motorClaim[m] = Nobody
    /\ motorClaim' = [motorClaim EXCEPT ![m] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<roomClaim, isolation, permitRound, standing>>

Isolate(b, m) ==
    /\ b \in standing
    /\ motorClaim[m] = b
    /\ isolation[m] = InService
    /\ isolation' = [isolation EXCEPT ![m] = [by |-> b, round |-> permitRound]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<roomClaim, motorClaim, permitRound, standing>>

Restore(b, m) ==
    /\ isolation[m] # InService
    /\ isolation[m].by = b
    /\ isolation' = [isolation EXCEPT ![m] = InService]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<roomClaim, motorClaim, permitRound, standing>>

\* Dropping the coarse claim leaves the fine ones standing behind it.
DropRoom(b) ==
    /\ roomClaim = b
    /\ roomClaim' = Nobody
    /\ UNCHANGED <<motorClaim, isolation, permitRound, standing>>

Orphaned == roomClaim = Nobody /\ \E m \in Motors : motorClaim[m] # Nobody

ClearOrphans ==
    /\ Orphaned
    /\ motorClaim' = [m \in Motors |-> Nobody]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<roomClaim, isolation, permitRound, standing>>

\* Nothing isolated under the old round survives a reissue.
Reissue ==
    /\ permitRound < MaxRound
    /\ permitRound' = permitRound + 1
    /\ isolation' = [m \in Motors |-> InService]
    /\ standing' = Banks
    /\ UNCHANGED <<roomClaim, motorClaim>>

Suspend(b) ==
    /\ b \in standing
    /\ Cardinality(standing) > 1
    /\ standing' = standing \ {b}
    /\ isolation' = [m \in Motors |->
                       IF isolation[m] # InService /\ isolation[m].by = b
                         THEN InService ELSE isolation[m]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<roomClaim, motorClaim, permitRound>>

Next ==
    \/ ClearOrphans \/ Reissue
    \/ \E b \in Banks :
         \/ TakeRoom(b) \/ DropRoom(b) \/ Suspend(b)
         \/ \E m \in Motors : TakeMotor(b, m) \/ Isolate(b, m) \/ Restore(b, m)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(ClearOrphans)

\* Nothing is held out of service by a suspended bank or an old permit.
IsolationsAreCurrent ==
    \A m \in Motors :
        isolation[m] # InService =>
            (isolation[m].by \in standing /\ isolation[m].round = permitRound)

\* Fine claims are never left orphaned for ever.
OrphansSweptUp == Orphaned ~> ~Orphaned

====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Banks = {bknorth, bksouth}
    Motors = {hm1, hm2}
    MaxRound = 1
    Nobody = nobody
    InService = inservice

INVARIANT IsolationsAreCurrent

PROPERTY OrphansSweptUp
nl:
A skyscraper has two elevator banks that run independently of one another but draw their hoist
motors from one shared machine room. Taking a motor out of service for work is done under a permit
system, and getting at a motor takes two claims, the coarse one before the fine one.

A bank's engineering desk first takes the machine-room claim, which only one of the two banks holds
at a time. Holding it, the desk may take a claim on individual motors. Only a desk holding a
motor's claim, and holding a permit, may isolate that motor; isolating records which bank did it
and which permit round was in force at the time. An isolated motor is put back into service by the
bank that isolated it.

Permits are reissued from time to time. Reissuing advances the permit round, restores every
isolated motor to service, and puts both banks back in good standing, because nothing isolated
under the old round may be left standing under the new one. A bank's permit can also be suspended
on its own, which puts back into service everything that bank had isolated; at least one bank is
always left in good standing.

Giving up the machine-room claim does not give up the motor claims taken under it, so motor claims
can be left standing with nobody holding the machine room. The building engineer sweeps up: when
the machine room is unclaimed but motor claims are still standing, they are all cleared away.

The full set of actions is: a bank in good standing takes the machine-room claim when it is free;
the bank holding the machine room takes a claim on a free motor; a bank in good standing isolates a
motor it has claimed, recording itself and the current permit round; a bank puts back into service
a motor it isolated; a bank gives up the machine-room claim, leaving its motor claims standing;
the building engineer clears away all standing motor claims while the machine room is unclaimed;
permits are reissued, advancing the round, restoring every motor and putting both banks in good
standing; and one bank's permit is suspended, restoring everything it had isolated, provided the
other bank is left in good standing.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every motor that is out of service was isolated by a bank that is still in good
standing and under the permit round that is currently in force, so no suspended bank and no
out-of-date permit ever holds a motor out of service.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Motor claims are never left orphaned for ever; whenever motor claims are
standing with the machine room unclaimed, they are eventually cleared away.

---- MODULE W4Od1m8p1t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Desks, Runways, Configs, Nothing, Nobody

ASSUME Nothing \notin Configs

VARIABLES fieldClaim, runwayClaim, published, inHand

vars == <<fieldClaim, runwayClaim, published, inHand>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ fieldClaim \in Desks \cup {Nobody}
    /\ runwayClaim \in [Runways -> Desks \cup {Nobody}]
    /\ published \in [Runways -> Configs]
    /\ inHand \in [Runways -> Configs \cup {Nothing}]

Init ==
    /\ fieldClaim = Nobody
    /\ runwayClaim = [r \in Runways |-> Nobody]
    /\ published = [r \in Runways |-> CHOOSE c \in Configs : TRUE]
    /\ inHand = [r \in Runways |-> Nothing]

TakeField(d) ==
    /\ fieldClaim = Nobody
    /\ fieldClaim' = d
    /\ UNCHANGED <<runwayClaim, published, inHand>>

\* Coarse before fine: no runway claim without the airfield-wide claim.
TakeRunway(d, r) ==
    /\ fieldClaim = d
    /\ runwayClaim[r] = Nobody
    /\ runwayClaim' = [runwayClaim EXCEPT ![r] = d]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fieldClaim, published, inHand>>

WriteDown(d, r, c) ==
    /\ runwayClaim[r] = d
    /\ inHand[r] = Nothing
    /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![r] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fieldClaim, runwayClaim, published>>

Publish(d, r) ==
    /\ runwayClaim[r] = d
    /\ inHand[r] # Nothing
    /\ published' = [published EXCEPT ![r] = inHand[r]]
    /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![r] = Nothing]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fieldClaim, runwayClaim>>

\* A desk cannot walk away from a runway with an amendment half-made.
GiveBackRunway(d, r) ==
    /\ runwayClaim[r] = d
    /\ inHand[r] = Nothing
    /\ runwayClaim' = [runwayClaim EXCEPT ![r] = Nobody]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fieldClaim, published, inHand>>

GiveBackField(d) ==
    /\ fieldClaim = d
    /\ \A r \in Runways : runwayClaim[r] # d
    /\ fieldClaim' = Nobody
    /\ UNCHANGED <<runwayClaim, published, inHand>>

\* The override finishes the amendment on its way out rather than dropping it.
Override(r) ==
    /\ runwayClaim[r] # Nobody
    /\ published' = IF inHand[r] # Nothing
                      THEN [published EXCEPT ![r] = inHand[r]]
                      ELSE published
    /\ inHand' = [inHand EXCEPT ![r] = Nothing]
    /\ runwayClaim' = [runwayClaim EXCEPT ![r] = Nobody]
    /\ UNCHANGED fieldClaim

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Runways : Override(r)
    \/ \E d \in Desks :
         \/ TakeField(d) \/ GiveBackField(d)
         \/ \E r \in Runways :
              \/ TakeRunway(d, r) \/ Publish(d, r) \/ GiveBackRunway(d, r)
              \/ \E c \in Configs : WriteDown(d, r, c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No amendment is ever stranded on a runway nobody is holding.
NoAmendmentStranded ==
    \A r \in Runways : runwayClaim[r] = Nobody => inHand[r] = Nothing

====
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator keeps one shared runway record. For each runway the record shows the
configuration currently published to the sectors, and amendments to it are made in two moves: the
amendment is first written down against that runway as the amendment in hand, and it is then
published, which is the move that changes what the record shows and clears the amendment in hand.
An amendment written down but not published is work in progress and is invisible to everybody
reading the record.

Getting at a runway takes two claims, coarse before fine. A sector desk first takes the
airfield-wide claim, which only one desk holds at a time. Holding it, the desk may take a claim on
an individual runway, and only the desk holding a runway's claim may write down or publish an
amendment for it. A desk gives a runway claim back only once it has nothing written down against
that runway, so it can never walk away leaving an amendment half-made. A desk gives the
airfield-wide claim back only once it is holding no runway claims at all.

The watch supervisor holds a privileged override and can prise a runway claim out of a desk's hands
without asking. Because an amendment left written down but unpublished would simply be lost, the
override publishes whatever was written down against that runway as it takes the claim away, and
only then leaves the runway unclaimed.

The full set of actions is: a desk takes the airfield-wide claim when it is free; the desk holding
the airfield-wide claim takes a claim on a free runway; the desk holding a runway's claim writes an
amendment down against that runway, when it has nothing written down there already; the desk
holding a runway's claim publishes what it wrote down, changing the record and clearing the
amendment in hand; a desk gives back a runway claim, only with nothing written down against it; a
desk gives back the airfield-wide claim, only while holding no runway claims; and the supervisor
overrides, publishing whatever was written down against a runway and leaving that runway unclaimed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No runway is ever left unclaimed with an amendment still written down against it
and not yet published, so no amendment is ever lost.

---- MODULE W4Od5m5p3t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Players, Seats, Regions, Fabric, NoPlayer, NoSeat, NoProposal, Empty

Proposal == [player : Players, seat : Seats]

VARIABLES book, mySeat, proposal, tally, fabric

vars == <<book, mySeat, proposal, tally, fabric>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ book \in [Seats -> Players \cup {NoPlayer}]
    /\ mySeat \in [Players -> Seats \cup {NoSeat}]
    /\ proposal \in Proposal \cup {NoProposal}
    /\ tally \subseteq Regions
    /\ fabric \in [Fabric -> Regions \cup {Empty}]

Carried == Cardinality(tally) * 2 > Cardinality(Regions)

Init ==
    /\ book = [s \in Seats |-> NoPlayer]
    /\ mySeat = [p \in Players |-> NoSeat]
    /\ proposal = NoProposal
    /\ tally = {}
    /\ fabric = [f \in Fabric |-> Empty]

PutUp(p, s) ==
    /\ proposal = NoProposal
    /\ mySeat[p] = NoSeat
    /\ book[s] = NoPlayer
    /\ proposal' = [player |-> p, seat |-> s]
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, mySeat, fabric>>

CastVote(v, f) ==
    /\ proposal # NoProposal
    /\ fabric[f] = Empty
    /\ v \notin tally
    /\ fabric' = [fabric EXCEPT ![f] = v]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, mySeat, proposal, tally>>

\* Votes arrive in any order; one that outlives its proposal is thrown away.
HandOver(f) ==
    /\ fabric[f] # Empty
    /\ IF proposal # NoProposal
         THEN tally' = tally \cup {fabric[f]}
         ELSE tally' = tally
    /\ fabric' = [fabric EXCEPT ![f] = Empty]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, mySeat, proposal>>

\* Both the seat and the player are re-checked at the moment of seating.
Carry ==
    /\ proposal # NoProposal
    /\ Carried
    /\ book[proposal.seat] = NoPlayer
    /\ mySeat[proposal.player] = NoSeat
    /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![proposal.seat] = proposal.player]
    /\ mySeat' = [mySeat EXCEPT ![proposal.player] = proposal.seat]
    /\ proposal' = NoProposal
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED fabric

Withdraw ==
    /\ proposal # NoProposal
    /\ proposal' = NoProposal
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, mySeat, fabric>>

Leave(p) ==
    /\ mySeat[p] # NoSeat
    /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![mySeat[p]] = NoPlayer]
    /\ mySeat' = [mySeat EXCEPT ![p] = NoSeat]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<proposal, tally, fabric>>

Next ==
    \/ Carry \/ Withdraw
    \/ \E f \in Fabric : HandOver(f)
    \/ \E p \in Players : Leave(p) \/ \E s \in Seats : PutUp(p, s)
    \/ \E v \in Regions, f \in Fabric : CastVote(v, f)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(Withdraw)

\* What a player thinks it has and what the book says never come apart.
BookAgreesWithPlayers ==
    \A p \in Players : mySeat[p] # NoSeat => book[mySeat[p]] = p

\* A part-finished ballot is never left standing for ever.
TallyAlwaysClears == (tally # {}) ~> (tally = {})

====
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker seats players into the lobby's numbered seats. The lobby keeps
a seating book saying which player is in each seat, and every player separately knows which seat it
has been given. A seat holds one player and a player sits in one seat.

Seating is decided by the region servers. The matchmaker puts up one proposal at a time, naming a
player with no seat and a seat the book shows empty. Region servers then vote on the proposal, and
their votes travel over the lobby's message fabric, which carries several votes at once and hands
them over in whatever order it happens to, not the order they were cast. A vote counts only when it
is handed over, and only if the proposal it was cast for is still the proposal on the table; a vote
that arrives after the proposal has gone is discarded rather than being counted towards whatever is
on the table now.

When a strict majority of region servers have votes recorded for the proposal on the table, and the
named seat is still empty and the named player still unseated at that moment, the player is seated:
the book is written and the player is told its seat. Putting a player in clears the proposal and
the recorded votes. A proposal can also be withdrawn, which clears it and the recorded votes
without seating anybody. A seated player can leave, which empties its seat in the book.

The full set of actions is: the matchmaker puts up a proposal naming an unseated player and an
empty seat; a region server casts its vote for the proposal onto a free place on the message
fabric; a vote is handed over off the fabric and recorded, but only if the proposal it was cast for
is still on the table; the proposal is carried and the player seated when a strict majority is
recorded and the seat and player are both still free, clearing the proposal and the votes; the
proposal is withdrawn, clearing it and the votes; and a seated player leaves, emptying its seat.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every player that believes it has a seat is the player the seating book shows in
that seat, so no seat is ever given out to two players at once.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Recorded votes never stand for ever; whenever any vote has been recorded, the
tally is eventually cleared.

---- MODULE W4Od13m3p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Routes, Machines, HopperDepth, Product, Nobody, NoMachine

ASSUME HopperDepth < Product

VARIABLES hopper, depot, controller, filling

vars == <<hopper, depot, controller, filling>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ hopper \in [Machines -> 0..Product]
    /\ depot \in 0..Product
    /\ controller \in Routes \cup {Nobody}
    /\ filling \in [Routes -> Machines \cup {NoMachine}]

Init ==
    /\ hopper = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
    /\ depot = Product
    /\ controller = Nobody
    /\ filling = [r \in Routes |-> NoMachine]

TakeRole(r) ==
    /\ controller = Nobody
    /\ controller' = r
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hopper, depot, filling>>

DropRole ==
    /\ controller # Nobody
    /\ controller' = Nobody
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hopper, depot, filling>>

\* Two routes never work the same machine at the same time.
OpenFill(r, m) ==
    /\ controller # Nobody
    /\ filling[r] = NoMachine
    /\ \A q \in Routes : filling[q] # m
    /\ filling' = [filling EXCEPT ![r] = m]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hopper, depot, controller>>

\* The depth is checked on every single unit, not once per fill.
LoadUnit(r) ==
    /\ filling[r] # NoMachine
    /\ depot > 0
    /\ hopper[filling[r]] < HopperDepth
    /\ hopper' = [hopper EXCEPT ![filling[r]] = @ + 1]
    /\ depot' = depot - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<controller, filling>>

CloseFill(r) ==
    /\ filling[r] # NoMachine
    /\ filling' = [filling EXCEPT ![r] = NoMachine]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hopper, depot, controller>>

Vend(m) ==
    /\ hopper[m] > 0
    /\ hopper' = [hopper EXCEPT ![m] = @ - 1]
    /\ depot' = depot + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<controller, filling>>

Next ==
    \/ DropRole
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Vend(m)
    \/ \E r \in Routes :
         \/ TakeRole(r) \/ LoadUnit(r) \/ CloseFill(r)
         \/ \E m \in Machines : OpenFill(r, m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No hopper is ever filled past its depth.
HoppersWithinDepth == \A m \in Machines : hopper[m] <= HopperDepth

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Routes = {rtnorth, rtsouth}
    Machines = {vm1, vm2}
    HopperDepth = 2
    Product = 4
    Nobody = nobody
    NoMachine = nomachine

INVARIANT HoppersWithinDepth
nl:
A vending machine network is worked by two restock routes. The routes run independently of each
other but draw their stock from one shared depot, and they fill the same set of machines. Each
machine has a hopper with a fixed depth, and a hopper must never be filled past that depth or the
mechanism jams.

Restocking is authorised by the network's route controller. One route acts as controller at a time;
when there is none, either route can take the role, and the sitting controller can drop it at any
moment, which is how the network carries on when a route's handset goes down. Nothing is restocked
while there is no controller.

A route opens a fill on a machine that the other route is not already filling, and then loads
product into it one unit at a time. Each unit loaded comes out of the shared depot and goes into
that machine's hopper, and a unit is only loaded if the hopper is below its depth at that moment.
The route closes the fill when it is done. Product sold out of a machine goes back to the depot as
the empties are collected, so the network's product neither appears from nowhere nor disappears.

The full set of actions is: a route takes the controller role when there is none; the sitting
controller drops the role; a route opens a fill on a machine that the other route is not filling,
provided there is a controller; a route loads one unit from the depot into the machine it is
filling, provided that hopper is below its depth; a route closes its fill; and a machine vends one
unit, which returns that unit to the depot.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No machine's hopper ever holds more units than the hopper's depth allows.

---- MODULE W4Od5m1p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS SiteCount, Tickets, MaxBatch, NoSite

Sites == 1..SiteCount

\* The ring order the permit travels in.
Downstream(s) == IF s = SiteCount THEN 1 ELSE s + 1

VARIABLES banked, inPlay, carrying, permitAt, onLink

vars == <<banked, inPlay, carrying, permitAt, onLink>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ banked \in [Sites -> 0..Tickets]
    /\ inPlay \in [Sites -> 0..Tickets]
    /\ carrying \in 0..Tickets
    /\ permitAt \in Sites \cup {NoSite}
    /\ onLink \in Sites \cup {NoSite}

RECURSIVE Total(_, _)
Total(S, f) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET s == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN f[s] + Total(S \ {s}, f)

Init ==
    /\ banked = [s \in Sites |-> IF s = 1 THEN Tickets ELSE 0]
    /\ inPlay = [s \in Sites |-> 0]
    /\ carrying = 0
    /\ permitAt = 1
    /\ onLink = NoSite

\* Picked-up tickets leave the bank at once and land only when set down.
PickUp(s, k) ==
    /\ permitAt = s
    /\ carrying = 0
    /\ banked[s] >= k
    /\ banked' = [banked EXCEPT ![s] = @ - k]
    /\ carrying' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inPlay, permitAt, onLink>>

SetDown(s) ==
    /\ permitAt = s
    /\ carrying > 0
    /\ banked' = [banked EXCEPT ![s] = @ + carrying]
    /\ carrying' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inPlay, permitAt, onLink>>

Commit(s, k) ==
    /\ permitAt = s
    /\ banked[s] >= k
    /\ banked' = [banked EXCEPT ![s] = @ - k]
    /\ inPlay' = [inPlay EXCEPT ![s] = @ + k]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<carrying, permitAt, onLink>>

ReturnToBank(s, k) ==
    /\ permitAt = s
    /\ inPlay[s] >= k
    /\ inPlay' = [inPlay EXCEPT ![s] = @ - k]
    /\ banked' = [banked EXCEPT ![s] = @ + k]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<carrying, permitAt, onLink>>

LetGo(s) ==
    /\ permitAt = s
    /\ permitAt' = NoSite
    /\ onLink' = Downstream(s)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<banked, inPlay, carrying>>

Arrive ==
    /\ onLink # NoSite
    /\ permitAt' = onLink
    /\ onLink' = NoSite
    /\ UNCHANGED <<banked, inPlay, carrying>>

LetGoSome == \E s \in Sites : LetGo(s)

Next ==
    \/ Arrive \/ LetGoSome
    \/ \E s \in Sites :
         \/ SetDown(s)
         \/ \E k \in 1..MaxBatch : PickUp(s, k) \/ Commit(s, k) \/ ReturnToBank(s, k)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(LetGoSome)

\* Every ticket is banked somewhere, in play somewhere, or on the permit.
TicketsConserved ==
    Total(Sites, banked) + Total(Sites, inPlay) + carrying = Tickets

\* No site sits on the permit for ever.
PermitKeepsMoving ==
    \A s \in Sites : (permitAt = s) ~> (permitAt # s)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    SiteCount = 3
    Tickets = 3
    MaxBatch = 2
    NoSite = 0

INVARIANT TicketsConserved

PROPERTY PermitKeepsMoving
nl:
A multiplayer game runs two lobby shards that are otherwise independent but share one pool of match
tickets. Tickets are the thing that lets a match run, and the operator neither mints nor destroys
them during a season, so at every moment every ticket is in exactly one place: banked at the ticket
pool or at one of the two shards, committed to a match in play at one of them, or riding on the
wire with the transfer permit.

Only one site may move tickets at a time, and the right to move them is a single permit that goes
round the three sites in a fixed ring order. The permit is either sitting at a site or travelling
down the link to the next site round, never at two sites and never nowhere. The site holding the
permit may pick up a batch of its banked tickets onto the permit, and may set down onto its own
bank whatever the permit is carrying. Picking up takes the tickets out of that site's bank the
moment it happens; they only land somewhere again when they are set down.

Also under the permit, a site may commit some of its banked tickets to matches in play, and may
return tickets from finished matches back to its bank.

The full set of actions is: the site holding the permit picks up a batch of its banked tickets onto
the permit, when the permit is carrying nothing; the site holding the permit sets down onto its own
bank whatever the permit is carrying; the site holding the permit commits a batch of its banked
tickets to matches in play; the site holding the permit returns a batch of tickets from play to its
bank; the site holding the permit lets it go onto the link to the next site round the ring; and a
permit travelling on a link arrives at the site it was sent to.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The tickets banked across the three sites, plus those committed to matches in play,
plus whatever the permit is carrying, always add up to exactly the season's fixed ticket count.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: No site keeps the permit for ever; whenever a site is holding it, the permit
eventually moves off that site.

---- MODULE W4Od17m6p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Scanners, Channels, LeaseTicks, LastNumber, Nobody, Idle, Empty

Stamped == [by : Scanners, number : 0..LastNumber]

VARIABLES owner, ticks, number, setting, busbar

vars == <<owner, ticks, number, setting, busbar>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ owner \in Scanners \cup {Nobody}
    /\ ticks \in 0..LeaseTicks
    /\ number \in 0..LastNumber
    /\ setting \in Stamped \cup {Idle}
    /\ busbar \in [Channels -> Stamped \cup {Empty}]

BusClear == \A c \in Channels : busbar[c] = Empty

Init ==
    /\ owner = Nobody
    /\ ticks = 0
    /\ number = 0
    /\ setting = Idle
    /\ busbar = [c \in Channels |-> Empty]

\* Every grant takes a fresh number, which is what dates the old ones.
Grant(n) ==
    /\ owner = Nobody
    /\ number < LastNumber
    /\ owner' = n
    /\ ticks' = LeaseTicks
    /\ number' = number + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<setting, busbar>>

\* Running out leaves nobody owning the chute and nothing set on it.
Tick ==
    /\ ticks > 0
    /\ ticks' = ticks - 1
    /\ owner' = IF ticks = 1 THEN Nobody ELSE owner
    /\ setting' = IF ticks = 1 THEN Idle ELSE setting
    /\ UNCHANGED <<number, busbar>>

Renew(n) ==
    /\ owner = n
    /\ ticks > 0
    /\ ticks' = LeaseTicks
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, number, setting, busbar>>

Post(n, c) ==
    /\ owner = n
    /\ ticks > 0
    /\ busbar[c] = Empty
    /\ busbar' = [busbar EXCEPT ![c] = [by |-> n, number |-> number]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ticks, number, setting>>

\* Name, lease number and a running lease must all still line up on arrival.
Apply(c) ==
    /\ busbar[c] # Empty
    /\ LET m == busbar[c] IN
         /\ IF owner = m.by /\ number = m.number /\ ticks > 0
              THEN setting' = m
              ELSE setting' = setting
         /\ busbar' = [busbar EXCEPT ![c] = Empty]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ticks, number>>

Wipe(n) ==
    /\ owner = n
    /\ setting # Idle
    /\ setting' = Idle
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ticks, number, busbar>>

HandBack(n) ==
    /\ owner = n
    /\ owner' = Nobody
    /\ ticks' = 0
    /\ setting' = Idle
    /\ UNCHANGED <<number, busbar>>

RestartNumbering ==
    /\ number = LastNumber
    /\ owner = Nobody
    /\ setting = Idle
    /\ BusClear
    /\ number' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, ticks, setting, busbar>>

Next ==
    \/ Tick \/ RestartNumbering
    \/ \E c \in Channels : Apply(c)
    \/ \E n \in Scanners :
         \/ Grant(n) \/ Renew(n) \/ Wipe(n) \/ HandBack(n)
         \/ \E c \in Channels : Post(n, c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Nothing governs the chute except the owner of the lease running right now.
SettingBackedByLiveLease ==
    setting # Idle =>
        (owner # Nobody /\ setting.by = owner /\ setting.number = number /\ ticks > 0)

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Scanners = {scnA, scnB}
    Channels = {fb1, fb2}
    LeaseTicks = 2
    LastNumber = 2
    Nobody = nobody
    Idle = idle
    Empty = empty

INVARIANT SettingBackedByLiveLease
nl:
An airport baggage router has one oversize chute whose diversion setting says where oversize items
are being sent. The setting is only ever written by whichever scanner node currently owns the
chute, and ownership is leased rather than permanent.

A lease is granted to a node when the chute is unowned, and each grant carries a fresh lease number,
one higher than the last. A lease runs for a fixed count of table ticks and counts down; the owner
can renew it while it is still running, which puts the count back to full without changing the lease
number. When the count reaches nothing the lease is over: the chute becomes unowned and its
diversion setting is wiped, because a setting with nobody behind it is not a setting anybody should
be routing to. The owner can also hand the lease back early, which does the same thing, and can
wipe the setting itself while still holding the lease.

Diversion instructions are not applied where they are written. The owner puts an instruction onto
the router's field bus, stamped with its own name and its lease number. The bus carries several
instructions at once and hands them to the chute in whatever order it gets to them, not the order
they were written, so an instruction can arrive long after the lease it was written under has run
out or been handed on. The chute applies an instruction only if the name on it is the node that
owns the chute right now, the lease number on it is the lease number running right now, and that
lease has not run out. Anything else is thrown away on arrival.

Lease numbers do not run for ever. When the numbering has reached its last value and the chute is
unowned, its setting wiped and the bus completely clear, the numbering starts again from the
beginning.

The full set of actions is: a node is granted the lease on the unowned chute, taking a fresh lease
number and a full count; the table ticks, counting the lease down and, if that exhausts it, leaving
the chute unowned with its setting wiped; the owner renews its lease back to a full count; the
owner puts a stamped instruction onto a free place on the field bus; the chute takes an instruction
off the bus and applies it only if the name, the lease number and the running lease all match,
throwing it away otherwise; the owner wipes the diversion setting; the owner hands the lease back
early, wiping the setting; and the lease numbering restarts once it has run out with nothing owned,
nothing set and the bus clear.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever the chute carries a diversion setting, it was written by the node that
owns the chute right now, under the lease number running right now, and that lease has not run out,
so no lapsed owner and no out-of-date instruction ever governs where oversize items go.

---- MODULE W4Od13m2p1t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Machines, Fields, Prices, MaxLog, NoChange

Change == [field : Fields, price : Prices]

VARIABLES list, changeLog, phase, ballot, proposal

vars == <<list, changeLog, phase, ballot, proposal>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ list \in [Fields -> Prices]
    /\ changeLog \in Seq(Change)
    /\ phase \in {"idle", "voting"}
    /\ ballot \in [Machines -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]
    /\ proposal \in Change \cup {NoChange}

Logged(f) == \E i \in DOMAIN changeLog : changeLog[i].field = f

\* The index of the most recent log entry touching this field.
Latest(f) ==
    CHOOSE i \in DOMAIN changeLog :
        /\ changeLog[i].field = f
        /\ \A j \in DOMAIN changeLog : changeLog[j].field = f => j <= i

Unanimous == \A m \in Machines : ballot[m] = "yes"

Init ==
    /\ list = [f \in Fields |-> CHOOSE p \in Prices : TRUE]
    /\ changeLog = << >>
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ ballot = [m \in Machines |-> "none"]
    /\ proposal = NoChange

PutUp(f, p) ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ proposal' = [field |-> f, price |-> p]
    /\ phase' = "voting"
    /\ ballot' = [m \in Machines |-> "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<list, changeLog>>

RecordVote(m, v) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ ballot[m] = "none"
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![m] = v]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<list, changeLog, phase, proposal>>

\* The log entry and the list are written in the same movement.
Apply ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ Unanimous
    /\ changeLog' = Append(changeLog, proposal)
    /\ list' = [list EXCEPT ![proposal.field] = proposal.price]
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ proposal' = NoChange
    /\ UNCHANGED ballot

Abandon ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ \E m \in Machines : ballot[m] = "no"
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ proposal' = NoChange
    /\ UNCHANGED <<list, changeLog, ballot>>

\* The override skips the vote but not the bookkeeping.
Force(f, p) ==
    /\ changeLog' = Append(changeLog, [field |-> f, price |-> p])
    /\ list' = [list EXCEPT ![f] = p]
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ proposal' = NoChange
    /\ UNCHANGED ballot

Next ==
    \/ Apply \/ Abandon
    \/ \E f \in Fields, p \in Prices : PutUp(f, p) \/ Force(f, p)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : RecordVote(m, "yes") \/ RecordVote(m, "no")

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(Apply)

Bounded == Len(changeLog) <= MaxLog

\* The list always shows the newest change the log has for that field.
ListShowsLatestChange ==
    \A f \in Fields : Logged(f) => list[f] = changeLog[Latest(f)].price

\* A change everyone has agreed to never sits there unapplied.
UnanimousRoundsFinish ==
    (phase = "voting" /\ Unanimous) ~> (phase = "idle")

====
nl:
A vending machine network runs off one shared price list. The list has a handful of price fields,
and head office keeps a change log recording, in order, every price change that has actually taken
effect. The list and the log are meant to tell the same story: for any field that has ever been
changed, the price the list shows is the price named by the most recent change to that field in the
log. A change that made it into the log but never reached the list would be a change the network
has silently lost.

A price change is not simply written. Head office puts up one proposed change at a time, naming a
field and a new price, and the machines then vote on it, each recording a yes or a no. When every
machine has voted yes the change is applied: it is appended to the change log and written onto the
price list in the same movement. If any machine has voted no the round is abandoned and nothing is
changed.

The regional manager holds a privileged override and can force a price onto a field without any
vote at all. The override, too, appends to the change log and writes the list together, and it ends
whatever round was in progress.

The full set of actions is: head office puts up a proposed change naming a field and a price; a
machine records a yes on the proposal; a machine records a no on the proposal; the change is
applied once every machine has recorded a yes, appending it to the log and writing it onto the
list; the round is abandoned once a machine has recorded a no; and the regional manager overrides,
appending a forced change to the log, writing it onto the list, and ending any round in progress.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every field that the change log has an entry for, the price list shows the
price named by that field's most recent log entry, so no change that reached the log is ever lost
from the list.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A proposal that every machine has voted yes on never sits unapplied; the round
always eventually ends.

---- MODULE W4Od16m7p4t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Technicians, Schedules, MaxUnits, MaxCeiling, NoRead, NoUnit

Reading == [sched : Schedules, figure : 0..MaxUnits]

VARIABLES onFloor, ceiling, remembered, carrying

vars == <<onFloor, ceiling, remembered, carrying>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ onFloor \in [Schedules -> 0..MaxUnits]
    /\ ceiling \in [Schedules -> 0..MaxCeiling]
    /\ remembered \in [Technicians -> Reading \cup {NoRead}]
    /\ carrying \in [Technicians -> Schedules \cup {NoUnit}]

Init ==
    /\ onFloor = [s \in Schedules |-> 0]
    /\ ceiling = [s \in Schedules |-> 1]
    /\ remembered = [t \in Technicians |-> NoRead]
    /\ carrying = [t \in Technicians |-> NoUnit]

\* The read holds nothing back; it only records what the counter said.
ReadCounter(t, s) ==
    /\ remembered[t] = NoRead
    /\ carrying[t] = NoUnit
    /\ remembered' = [remembered EXCEPT ![t] = [sched |-> s, figure |-> onFloor[s]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onFloor, ceiling, carrying>>

\* The draw lands only on an untouched counter and under the current ceiling.
Draw(t) ==
    /\ remembered[t] # NoRead
    /\ carrying[t] = NoUnit
    /\ onFloor[remembered[t].sched] = remembered[t].figure
    /\ remembered[t].figure < ceiling[remembered[t].sched]
    /\ onFloor' = [onFloor EXCEPT ![remembered[t].sched] = remembered[t].figure + 1]
    /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![t] = remembered[t].sched]
    /\ remembered' = [remembered EXCEPT ![t] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED ceiling

Reread(t) ==
    /\ remembered[t] # NoRead
    /\ onFloor[remembered[t].sched] # remembered[t].figure
    /\ remembered' = [remembered EXCEPT ![t] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onFloor, ceiling, carrying>>

Return(t) ==
    /\ carrying[t] # NoUnit
    /\ onFloor[carrying[t]] > 0
    /\ onFloor' = [onFloor EXCEPT ![carrying[t]] = @ - 1]
    /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![t] = NoUnit]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ceiling, remembered>>

Raise(s) ==
    /\ ceiling[s] < MaxCeiling
    /\ ceiling' = [ceiling EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onFloor, remembered, carrying>>

\* A ceiling only comes down while it is above what is already out.
Lower(s) ==
    /\ ceiling[s] > onFloor[s]
    /\ ceiling' = [ceiling EXCEPT ![s] = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onFloor, remembered, carrying>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Schedules : Raise(s) \/ Lower(s)
    \/ \E t \in Technicians :
         \/ Draw(t) \/ Reread(t) \/ Return(t)
         \/ \E s \in Schedules : ReadCounter(t, s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No schedule ever has more units out than its ceiling currently allows.
FloorWithinCeilings == \A s \in Schedules : onFloor[s] <= ceiling[s]

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Technicians = {tcha, tchb}
    Schedules = {sch2, sch3}
    MaxUnits = 3
    MaxCeiling = 2
    NoRead = noread
    NoUnit = nounit

INVARIANT FloorWithinCeilings
nl:
A pharmacy's dispenser holds controlled drugs of more than one schedule, and each schedule has its
own ceiling on how many units of it may be out on the dispensing floor at once. The ceilings are
not fixed: the responsible pharmacist raises and lowers them during the day as the licence and the
staffing allow. A ceiling is only ever lowered while it is strictly above the number of units of
that schedule currently out, so lowering never strands units outside the new ceiling.

For each schedule the dispenser keeps one counter of how many units of it are out. A technician
drawing a unit does not lock the counter. It reads the counter for the schedule it wants and
remembers both which schedule and what figure it saw. When it goes to draw, the draw only goes
through if that schedule's counter still reads exactly the figure remembered, and if that figure is
below the schedule's ceiling as it stands at that moment; the counter then goes up by one and the
technician has the unit. If another technician has drawn or returned in the meantime the counter no
longer matches the remembered figure, so the reading is thrown away and the technician reads again.

A technician carries at most one unit at a time and returns it when the dispensing is done, which
brings that schedule's counter back down by one.

The full set of actions is: a technician carrying nothing reads the counter for a schedule and
remembers the schedule and the figure; a technician draws a unit, provided the counter still reads
the remembered figure and that figure is below the schedule's current ceiling; a technician whose
remembered figure no longer matches the counter throws the reading away; a technician returns the
unit it is carrying, bringing that schedule's counter down; the pharmacist raises a schedule's
ceiling; and the pharmacist lowers a schedule's ceiling, only while it is above the units of that
schedule currently out.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every schedule, the number of units of that schedule out on the dispensing
floor never exceeds that schedule's ceiling as it currently stands.

---- MODULE W4Od0m5p4t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Theatres, Consultants, Cover, Beats, NoTheatre

VARIABLES running, signed, request, thinking

vars == <<running, signed, request, thinking>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ running \subseteq Theatres
    /\ signed \in [Consultants -> Theatres \cup {NoTheatre}]
    /\ request \in Theatres \cup {NoTheatre}
    /\ thinking \in [Consultants -> 0..Beats]

Deliberating == \E c \in Consultants : thinking[c] > 0

Backing == Cardinality({c \in Consultants : signed[c] = request /\ request # NoTheatre})

Majority == Backing * 2 > Cardinality(Consultants)

Init ==
    /\ running = {}
    /\ signed = [c \in Consultants |-> NoTheatre]
    /\ request = NoTheatre
    /\ thinking = [c \in Consultants |-> 0]

\* Nothing new goes up while the panel is still chewing on the last one.
Raise(th) ==
    /\ request = NoTheatre
    /\ ~Deliberating
    /\ th \notin running
    /\ request' = th
    /\ signed' = [c \in Consultants |-> NoTheatre]
    /\ thinking' = [c \in Consultants |-> Beats]
    /\ UNCHANGED running

\* One clock counts every consultant still deliberating down together.
Beat ==
    /\ Deliberating
    /\ thinking' = [c \in Consultants |-> IF thinking[c] > 0 THEN thinking[c] - 1 ELSE 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<running, signed, request>>

Sign(c) ==
    /\ request # NoTheatre
    /\ thinking[c] = 0
    /\ signed[c] # request
    /\ signed' = [signed EXCEPT ![c] = request]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<running, request, thinking>>

\* The cover is re-checked at the moment the theatre opens.
Open ==
    /\ request # NoTheatre
    /\ Majority
    /\ Cardinality(running) < Cover
    /\ running' = running \cup {request}
    /\ request' = NoTheatre
    /\ UNCHANGED <<signed, thinking>>

Withdraw ==
    /\ request # NoTheatre
    /\ request' = NoTheatre
    /\ UNCHANGED <<running, signed, thinking>>

Close(th) ==
    /\ th \in running
    /\ running' = running \ {th}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<signed, request, thinking>>

Next ==
    \/ Beat \/ Open \/ Withdraw
    \/ \E th \in Theatres : Raise(th) \/ Close(th)
    \/ \E c \in Consultants : Sign(c)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(Beat)

\* Never more theatres running than there is anaesthetic cover for.
RunningWithinCover == Cardinality(running) <= Cover

\* Deliberation always runs out in the end.
DeliberationEnds == Deliberating ~> ~Deliberating

====

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Theatres = {thr1, thr2, thr3}
    Consultants = {cna, cnb, cnc}
    Cover = 2
    Beats = 2
    NoTheatre = notheatre

INVARIANT RunningWithinCover

PROPERTY DeliberationEnds
nl:
A hospital's operating-room scheduler decides which theatres are open at any moment. The limit is
not the theatres themselves but the anaesthetic cover: only a fixed number of theatres can be
running at once, because that is how many anaesthetists the hospital has on the floor.

Opening a theatre needs the consultants' panel behind it. The scheduler raises one request at a
time, naming a theatre that is not already running. Each consultant on the panel then signs the
request. Consultants do not all work at the same speed: when a request goes up, every consultant
starts a period of deliberation, and a consultant cannot sign until its own deliberation has run
out. Deliberation runs on the panel's clock, which counts down every consultant still deliberating
together, a beat at a time. Nobody is ever stuck: a slow consultant simply has more beats to get
through, and every consultant's deliberation always runs out in the end. The scheduler will not
raise a new request while any consultant is still deliberating on the one in hand.

The theatre opens when a strict majority of the panel have signed the request and the anaesthetic
cover has room for one more theatre at that moment. Opening clears the request. A request can also
be withdrawn without opening anything. A running theatre can be closed, which gives its anaesthetic
cover back.

The full set of actions is: the scheduler raises a request naming a theatre that is not running,
which starts every consultant deliberating, and which it may only do while nobody is deliberating;
the panel clock beats, counting down every consultant still deliberating; a consultant whose
deliberation has run out signs the request in hand; the theatre opens when a strict majority have
signed and the anaesthetic cover has room, clearing the request; the request is withdrawn without
opening anything; and a running theatre is closed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of theatres running at once never exceeds the hospital's anaesthetic
cover.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The panel never deliberates for ever; whenever any consultant is deliberating,
deliberation eventually runs out for all of them.

---- MODULE W4Od14m9p1t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Segments, MaxGeneration, MaxBudget

Observation == [seg : Segments, gen : 0..MaxGeneration]

VARIABLES carried, budget, file, shown, generation

vars == <<carried, budget, file, shown, generation>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ carried \subseteq Segments
    /\ budget \in 0..MaxBudget
    /\ file \subseteq Observation
    /\ shown \in [Segments -> 0..MaxGeneration]
    /\ generation \in 0..MaxGeneration

GensFor(g) == {o.gen : o \in {x \in file : x.seg = g}}

\* The latest generation the file holds for a segment.
Latest(g) == CHOOSE e \in GensFor(g) : \A f \in GensFor(g) : f <= e

Init ==
    /\ carried = {}
    /\ budget = 1
    /\ file = {}
    /\ shown = [g \in Segments |-> 0]
    /\ generation = 0

\* Coming back onto the map picks up from what the file already holds.
BringOn(g) ==
    /\ g \notin carried
    /\ Cardinality(carried) < budget
    /\ carried' = carried \cup {g}
    /\ shown' = [shown EXCEPT ![g] = IF GensFor(g) = {} THEN 0 ELSE Latest(g)]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<budget, file, generation>>

\* Within a segment the filed generations only ever climb.
Accept(g) ==
    /\ g \in carried
    /\ \A e \in GensFor(g) : e < generation
    /\ file' = file \cup {[seg |-> g, gen |-> generation]}
    /\ shown' = [shown EXCEPT ![g] = generation]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<carried, budget, generation>>

DropOff(g) ==
    /\ g \in carried
    /\ carried' = carried \ {g}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<budget, file, shown, generation>>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ generation < MaxGeneration
    /\ generation' = generation + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<carried, budget, file, shown>>

RaiseBudget ==
    /\ budget < MaxBudget
    /\ budget' = budget + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<carried, file, shown, generation>>

\* The budget only comes down above what the map is already carrying.
CutBudget ==
    /\ budget > Cardinality(carried)
    /\ budget > 0
    /\ budget' = budget - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<carried, file, shown, generation>>

Next ==
    \/ Reconfigure \/ RaiseBudget \/ CutBudget
    \/ \E g \in Segments : BringOn(g) \/ Accept(g) \/ DropOff(g)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Nothing filed for a carried segment is ever missing from the map.
MapShowsLatestFiled ==
    \A g \in carried : GensFor(g) # {} => shown[g] = Latest(g)

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Segments = {segN, segE}
    MaxGeneration = 2
    MaxBudget = 2

INVARIANT MapShowsLatestFiled
nl:
A wildfire drone swarm maintains a shared perimeter map. The fire's edge is divided into segments,
and for each segment the swarm records how far the edge has been observed to have moved. The swarm
also keeps the raw observation file: every observation the swarm has accepted, tagged with the
segment it was for and the swarm generation it was made in.

The swarm reconfigures as aircraft join and drop out, and each reconfiguration advances the swarm
generation. Observations are stamped with the generation current when they are accepted, and a
segment only accepts an observation whose generation is strictly later than every observation
already in the file for that segment, so within a segment the file's generations only ever climb.

The map does not carry every segment. It has a carrying budget -- how many segments it can hold
open at once -- and the flight director changes that budget during the incident as bandwidth
allows. The budget is only ever cut back while it is strictly above the number of segments the map
is currently carrying. Bringing a segment onto the map is only possible while the map is under its
budget, and a segment can be dropped off the map at any time. Dropping a segment does not throw
away its observations: the file keeps them, so when that segment is later brought back onto the
map, the map must pick up again from the latest generation the file already holds for it, not from
nothing.

The full set of actions is: a segment not on the map is brought onto it, provided the map is under
its carrying budget, and the map picks that segment up at the latest generation the observation
file already holds for it; an observation for a segment on the map is accepted and filed, stamped
with the current swarm generation, provided that generation is later than everything already filed
for that segment; a segment is dropped off the map, leaving its observations in the file; the swarm
reconfigures, advancing the generation; the flight director raises the carrying budget; and the
flight director cuts the carrying budget back, only while it is above the segments currently
carried.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every segment the map is carrying that has anything at all in the observation
file, the map shows exactly the latest generation the file holds for that segment, so no accepted
observation is ever lost from the map.

---- MODULE W4Od13m8p1t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Desks, Machines, MaxStock, MaxFigure, Nobody, Blank

VARIABLES regionClaim, machineClaim, slip, record

vars == <<regionClaim, machineClaim, slip, record>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ regionClaim \in Desks \cup {Nobody}
    /\ machineClaim \in [Machines -> Desks \cup {Nobody}]
    /\ slip \in [Machines -> (1..MaxFigure) \cup {Blank}]
    /\ record \in [Machines -> 0..MaxStock]

Init ==
    /\ regionClaim = Nobody
    /\ machineClaim = [m \in Machines |-> Nobody]
    /\ slip = [m \in Machines |-> Blank]
    /\ record = [m \in Machines |-> 0]

TakeRegion(d) ==
    /\ regionClaim = Nobody
    /\ regionClaim' = d
    /\ UNCHANGED <<machineClaim, slip, record>>

\* Coarse before fine: no machine claim without the region claim.
TakeMachine(d, m) ==
    /\ regionClaim = d
    /\ machineClaim[m] = Nobody
    /\ machineClaim' = [machineClaim EXCEPT ![m] = d]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<regionClaim, slip, record>>

WriteSlip(d, m, k) ==
    /\ regionClaim = d
    /\ machineClaim[m] = d
    /\ slip[m] = Blank
    /\ record[m] + k <= MaxStock
    /\ slip' = [slip EXCEPT ![m] = k]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<regionClaim, machineClaim, record>>

Post(d, m) ==
    /\ machineClaim[m] = d
    /\ slip[m] # Blank
    /\ record' = [record EXCEPT ![m] = @ + slip[m]]
    /\ slip' = [slip EXCEPT ![m] = Blank]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<regionClaim, machineClaim>>

\* Neither claim comes off while a figure is still sitting underneath it.
GiveBackMachine(d, m) ==
    /\ machineClaim[m] = d
    /\ slip[m] = Blank
    /\ machineClaim' = [machineClaim EXCEPT ![m] = Nobody]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<regionClaim, slip, record>>

GiveBackRegion(d) ==
    /\ regionClaim = d
    /\ \A m \in Machines : machineClaim[m] # d
    /\ regionClaim' = Nobody
    /\ UNCHANGED <<machineClaim, slip, record>>

\* The override posts everything on its way out rather than stranding it.
PullRegion ==
    /\ regionClaim # Nobody
    /\ record' = [m \in Machines |->
                    IF slip[m] # Blank THEN record[m] + slip[m] ELSE record[m]]
    /\ slip' = [m \in Machines |-> Blank]
    /\ machineClaim' = [m \in Machines |-> Nobody]
    /\ regionClaim' = Nobody

Next ==
    \/ PullRegion
    \/ \E d \in Desks :
         \/ TakeRegion(d) \/ GiveBackRegion(d)
         \/ \E m \in Machines :
              \/ TakeMachine(d, m) \/ Post(d, m) \/ GiveBackMachine(d, m)
              \/ \E k \in 1..MaxFigure : WriteSlip(d, m, k)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(PullRegion)

\* A figure waiting to be posted always has the whole chain of claims behind it.
SlipsSitUnderFullChain ==
    \A m \in Machines :
        slip[m] # Blank => (machineClaim[m] # Nobody /\ regionClaim = machineClaim[m])

\* Figures never sit on slips for ever.
SlipsAlwaysClear ==
    (\E m \in Machines : slip[m] # Blank) ~> (\A m \in Machines : slip[m] = Blank)

CONSTANTS
    Desks = {dska, dskb}
    Machines = {mch1, mch2}
    MaxStock = 3
    MaxFigure = 2
    Nobody = nobody
    Blank = blank

INVARIANT SlipsSitUnderFullChain

PROPERTY SlipsAlwaysClear
nl:
A vending machine network keeps one shared stock record with a line for every machine. Restock
figures are entered against a machine in two moves: the figure is first put on the slip for that
machine, and it is then posted, which is the move that changes the machine's line in the record and
clears the slip. A figure sitting on a slip is work in progress and nobody reading the record sees
it.

Getting at a machine's line takes two claims, coarse before fine. A route desk first takes the
region claim, which only one desk holds at a time. Holding the region claim, it may take a claim on
an individual machine, and only a desk holding both the region claim and that machine's claim may
put a figure on the slip. A desk gives a machine claim back only with that machine's slip clear,
and gives the region claim back only while it holds no machine claims at all, so the two claims can
never come apart underneath a slip that still has a figure on it.

Head office holds a privileged override and can pull the region claim back to itself without
asking. Pulling it back would strand every machine claim underneath, and any figure still sitting
on a slip would simply vanish, so the override posts every outstanding slip into the record as it
goes, clears all the slips, and releases every machine claim, leaving the region unclaimed and the
record complete.

The full set of actions is: a desk takes the region claim when it is free; the desk holding the
region claim takes a claim on a free machine; a desk holding the region claim and a machine's claim
puts a restock figure on that machine's slip, when the slip is clear and the figure fits the line;
a desk holding a machine's claim posts what is on the slip, changing the record and clearing the
slip; a desk gives back a machine claim, only with its slip clear; a desk gives back the region
claim, only while holding no machine claims; and head office pulls the region claim back, posting
every outstanding slip into the record, clearing every slip and releasing every machine claim.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any machine whose slip still carries a figure is claimed by a desk that also holds
the region claim, so a figure waiting to be posted is never left underneath a broken chain of
claims.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A figure never sits on a slip for ever; whenever any slip carries a figure, all
the slips are eventually cleared.

CONSTANTS Cars, Bays, Sensors, LastDocket, Outside, NoCar, NoRequest

Docketed == [bay : Bays, docket : 1..LastDocket]
Request == [car : Cars, bay : Bays]

VARIABLES sitting, counter, backing, request

vars == <<sitting, counter, backing, request>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ sitting \in [Cars -> Docketed \cup {Outside}]
    /\ counter \in [Bays -> 0..LastDocket]
    /\ backing \in [Sensors -> Cars \cup {NoCar}]
    /\ request \in Request \cup {NoRequest}

Backers(c) == Cardinality({s \in Sensors : backing[s] = c})

Majority(c) == Backers(c) * 2 > Cardinality(Sensors)

BayEmpty(b) ==
    \A c \in Cars : IF sitting[c] = Outside THEN TRUE ELSE sitting[c].bay # b

Init ==
    /\ sitting = [c \in Cars |-> Outside]
    /\ counter = [b \in Bays |-> 0]
    /\ backing = [s \in Sensors |-> NoCar]
    /\ request = NoRequest

Raise(c, b) ==
    /\ request = NoRequest
    /\ sitting[c] = Outside
    /\ request' = [car |-> c, bay |-> b]
    /\ backing' = [s \in Sensors |-> NoCar]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sitting, counter>>

Back(s) ==
    /\ request # NoRequest
    /\ backing[s] # request.car
    /\ backing' = [backing EXCEPT ![s] = request.car]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sitting, counter, request>>

\* Handing the bay out moves its docket number on and stamps the car with it.
Carry ==
    /\ request # NoRequest
    /\ Majority(request.car)
    /\ BayEmpty(request.bay)
    /\ counter[request.bay] < LastDocket
    /\ counter' = [counter EXCEPT ![request.bay] = @ + 1]
    /\ sitting' = [sitting EXCEPT ![request.car] =
                     [bay |-> request.bay, docket |-> counter[request.bay] + 1]]
    /\ request' = NoRequest
    /\ UNCHANGED backing

Withdraw ==
    /\ request # NoRequest
    /\ request' = NoRequest
    /\ backing' = [s \in Sensors |-> NoCar]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sitting, counter>>

Leave(c) ==
    /\ sitting[c] # Outside
    /\ sitting' = [sitting EXCEPT ![c] = Outside]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<counter, backing, request>>

Next ==
    \/ Carry \/ Withdraw
    \/ \E s \in Sensors : Back(s)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Leave(c) \/ \E b \in Bays : Raise(c, b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A car is in a bay only on that bay's current docket number.
DocketsAreCurrent ==

        IF sitting[c] = Outside THEN TRUE
        ELSE sitting[c].docket = counter[sitting[c].bay]

====
nl:
A car-wash site runs two conveyor lines that work independently but feed one shared pool of wash
bays. Each line presents one car at a time to the pool, and a car can only go into a bay that the
pool hands it.

A bay is not handed out on anybody's say-so. The site's bay sensors vote: a request names one car
and one bay, and the sensors then back that car one at a time. A request carries when a strict
majority of the sensors are backing its car and the named bay has nobody in it.

Every hand-out is written as a docket. Each bay has a docket number that goes up by one every time
that bay is handed out, and the car that got it keeps the docket number it was given. A car's
docket is what entitles it to be in the bay: the moment the bay is handed out again the bay's
number moves on, and any older docket for that bay is worth nothing. Docket numbers for a bay run
out after a while, and once they have, that bay is not handed out again.

A car in a bay leaves when its wash is done, freeing the bay. A request can also be withdrawn
before it carries, which clears the backing without handing anything out.

The full set of actions is: a request is raised naming a car that is in no bay and a bay from the
pool, clearing the backing; a sensor backs the car named in the request; the request carries when a
strict majority of sensors back its car, the named bay is empty and that bay has docket numbers
left, which moves the bay's docket number on and gives the car that number; the request is
withdrawn, clearing the backing; and a car in a bay leaves, freeing it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every car sitting in a bay holds exactly the docket number that bay's counter
currently shows, so a bay never has a car in it on a docket that has been superseded and never has
two cars in it at once.

ASSUME Nobody \notin Foremen

VARIABLES warrant, handedBy, yardClaim, rowClaim, working

vars == <<warrant, handedBy, yardClaim, rowClaim, working>>

    /\ warrant \in Foremen \cup {Nobody}
    /\ handedBy \in [Foremen -> Foremen \cup {Nobody}]
    /\ yardClaim \in Foremen \cup {Nobody}
    /\ rowClaim \in [Rows -> Foremen \cup {Nobody}]
    /\ working \in [Rows -> Foremen \cup {Nobody}]

\* Authority is live only while the person who handed it down still sits.
Live(f) == warrant # Nobody /\ handedBy[f] = warrant

Init ==
    /\ warrant = Nobody
    /\ handedBy = [f \in Foremen |-> Nobody]
    /\ yardClaim = Nobody
    /\ rowClaim = [r \in Rows |-> Nobody]
    /\ working = [r \in Rows |-> Nobody]

TakeWarrant(f) ==

    /\ UNCHANGED <<handedBy, yardClaim, rowClaim, working>>

HandDown(f) ==
    /\ warrant # Nobody
    /\ handedBy[f] = Nobody
    /\ handedBy' = [handedBy EXCEPT ![f] = warrant]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<warrant, yardClaim, rowClaim, working>>

TakeBack(f) ==
    /\ handedBy[f] # Nobody
    /\ handedBy' = [handedBy EXCEPT ![f] = Nobody]
    /\ working' = [r \in Rows |-> IF working[r] = f THEN Nobody ELSE working[r]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<warrant, yardClaim, rowClaim>>

TakeYard(f) ==
    /\ Live(f)
    /\ yardClaim = Nobody
    /\ yardClaim' = f
    /\ UNCHANGED <<warrant, handedBy, rowClaim, working>>

TakeRow(f, r) ==
    /\ yardClaim = f
    /\ rowClaim[r] = Nobody
    /\ rowClaim' = [rowClaim EXCEPT ![r] = f]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<warrant, handedBy, yardClaim, working>>

StartWork(f, r) ==
    /\ Live(f)
    /\ rowClaim[r] = f
    /\ working[r] = Nobody
    /\ working' = [working EXCEPT ![r] = f]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<warrant, handedBy, yardClaim, rowClaim>>

StopWork(f, r) ==
    /\ working[r] = f
    /\ working' = [working EXCEPT ![r] = Nobody]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<warrant, handedBy, yardClaim, rowClaim>>

\* A row claim never comes off from under work that is still running.
GiveBackRow(f, r) ==
    /\ rowClaim[r] = f
    /\ working[r] = Nobody
    /\ rowClaim' = [rowClaim EXCEPT ![r] = Nobody]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<warrant, handedBy, yardClaim, working>>

GiveBackYard(f) ==
    /\ yardClaim = f
    /\ yardClaim' = Nobody
    /\ UNCHANGED <<warrant, handedBy, rowClaim, working>>

\* The harbourmaster's override unseats the warrant outright, which voids
\* everything that was handed down under it and stops all work.
Override ==
    /\ warrant # Nobody
    /\ warrant' = Nobody
    /\ handedBy' = [f \in Foremen |-> Nobody]
    /\ working' = [r \in Rows |-> Nobody]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<yardClaim, rowClaim>>

Unbacked == yardClaim # Nobody /\ ~Live(yardClaim)

SweepYard ==
    /\ Unbacked
    /\ yardClaim' = Nobody
    /\ UNCHANGED <<warrant, handedBy, rowClaim, working>>

Next ==
    \/ Override \/ SweepYard
    \/ \E f \in Foremen :
         \/ TakeWarrant(f) \/ HandDown(f) \/ TakeBack(f) \/ TakeYard(f)
         \/ GiveBackYard(f)
         \/ \E r \in Rows : TakeRow(f, r) \/ StartWork(f, r)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(SweepYard)

\* Work only ever runs under a claim held by a foreman with live authority.
WorkRunsUnderLiveAuthority ==
    \A r \in Rows :

\* The yard-wide claim is never left with somebody who has no authority.
UnbackedYardClaimSwept == Unbacked ~> ~Unbacked

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Foremen = {fmna, fmnb}
    Rows = {rowA, rowB}
    Nobody = nobody

INVARIANT WorkRunsUnderLiveAuthority

PROPERTY UnbackedYardClaimSwept
nl:
A container-ship crane yard is worked in rows, and who may work a row runs down a chain of
authority. One gang foreman at a time holds the superintendent's warrant. The sitting
superintendent hands authority down to individual foremen; a foreman's authority is only worth
anything while the person who handed it down is still the sitting superintendent, so when the
warrant changes hands every authority handed down under the old holder is worth nothing.

Getting at a row takes two claims, coarse before fine. A foreman with live authority takes the
yard-wide claim, which only one foreman holds at a time. Holding it, the foreman takes claims on
individual rows. Work on a row can only be started by the foreman holding that row's claim and only
while that foreman's authority is live, and a row's claim cannot be given back while work on it is
still running.

Authority can be taken back from a foreman on its own, and taking it back stops whatever that
foreman had running. The harbourmaster holds a privileged override and can unseat the sitting
superintendent outright, without the yard's agreement: doing so leaves nobody holding the warrant,
voids every authority that was handed down under it and stops all work in the yard, until some
foreman takes the warrant up again.

Because the yard-wide claim can be left in the hands of a foreman whose authority has since gone,
the yard clerk sweeps up: whenever the yard-wide claim is held by somebody with no live authority,
the claim is taken back off them.

The full set of actions is: a foreman takes the superintendent's warrant when nobody holds it;
the sitting superintendent hands authority down to a foreman; authority is taken back from a
foreman, stopping its work; a foreman with live authority takes the yard-wide claim; the holder of
the yard-wide claim takes a claim on a free row; a foreman with live authority starts work on a row
it has claimed; a foreman stops work on a row; a foreman gives back a row claim with no work
running on it; a foreman gives back the yard-wide claim; the harbourmaster overrides,
unseating the sitting superintendent, voiding all authority and stopping all work; and the yard
clerk takes the yard-wide claim off a holder with no live authority.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every row with work running on it is being worked by the foreman holding that
row's claim, and that foreman's authority was handed down by the superintendent sitting right now,
so no foreman without live authority and no authority from a past superintendent ever has work
running.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The yard-wide claim never stays in the hands of a foreman without live
authority; whenever it is, it is eventually taken back off them.

---- MODULE W4Od18m8p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Fitters, Slots, Guests, MaxAllowance, Nobody, Blank, NoCode

VARIABLES hubClaim, slotClaim, programmed, code, allowance

vars == <<hubClaim, slotClaim, programmed, code, allowance>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ hubClaim \in Fitters \cup {Nobody}
    /\ slotClaim \in [Slots -> Fitters \cup {Nobody}]
    /\ programmed \in [Slots -> Guests \cup {Blank}]
    /\ code \in [Guests -> Slots \cup {NoCode}]
    /\ allowance \in 0..MaxAllowance

InUse == Cardinality({s \in Slots : programmed[s] # Blank})

Init ==
    /\ hubClaim = Nobody
    /\ slotClaim = [s \in Slots |-> Nobody]
    /\ programmed = [s \in Slots |-> Blank]
    /\ code = [g \in Guests |-> NoCode]
    /\ allowance = 1

TakeHub(f) ==
    /\ hubClaim = Nobody
    /\ hubClaim' = f
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotClaim, programmed, code, allowance>>

\* Coarse before fine: no slot claim without the hub claim.
TakeSlot(f, s) ==
    /\ hubClaim = f
    /\ slotClaim[s] = Nobody
    /\ slotClaim' = [slotClaim EXCEPT ![s] = f]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hubClaim, programmed, code, allowance>>

Programme(f, s, g) ==
    /\ slotClaim[s] = f
    /\ programmed[s] = Blank
    /\ code[g] = NoCode
    /\ InUse < allowance
    /\ programmed' = [programmed EXCEPT ![s] = g]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hubClaim, slotClaim, code, allowance>>

HandOverCode(f, s) ==
    /\ slotClaim[s] = f
    /\ programmed[s] # Blank
    /\ code[programmed[s]] = NoCode
    /\ code' = [code EXCEPT ![programmed[s]] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hubClaim, slotClaim, programmed, allowance>>

\* Wiping the slot cancels the outstanding code in the same movement.
Wipe(f, s) ==
    /\ slotClaim[s] = f
    /\ programmed[s] # Blank
    /\ code' = [code EXCEPT ![programmed[s]] = NoCode]
    /\ programmed' = [programmed EXCEPT ![s] = Blank]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hubClaim, slotClaim, allowance>>

GiveBackSlot(f, s) ==
    /\ slotClaim[s] = f
    /\ slotClaim' = [slotClaim EXCEPT ![s] = Nobody]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hubClaim, programmed, code, allowance>>

GiveBackHub(f) ==
    /\ hubClaim = f
    /\ \A s \in Slots : slotClaim[s] # f
    /\ hubClaim' = Nobody
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slotClaim, programmed, code, allowance>>

RaiseAllowance ==
    /\ allowance < MaxAllowance
    /\ allowance' = allowance + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hubClaim, slotClaim, programmed, code>>

\* The allowance only comes down above what is already programmed.
LowerAllowance ==
    /\ allowance > InUse
    /\ allowance > 0
    /\ allowance' = allowance - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hubClaim, slotClaim, programmed, code>>

Next ==
    \/ RaiseAllowance \/ LowerAllowance
    \/ \E f \in Fitters :
         \/ TakeHub(f) \/ GiveBackHub(f)
         \/ \E s \in Slots :
              \/ TakeSlot(f, s) \/ HandOverCode(f, s) \/ Wipe(f, s) \/ GiveBackSlot(f, s)
              \/ \E g \in Guests : Programme(f, s, g)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A guest's code always names a slot the lock still holds that guest in.
CodesMatchProgramming ==
    \A g \in Guests : code[g] # NoCode => programmed[code[g]] = g

====
nl:
A smart-home door lock network gives visitors entry through guest code slots. Each slot on the lock
can be programmed with one guest, and a guest who has been given a code knows which slot that code
belongs to. The lock's own programming and what the guests have been told are meant to agree
exactly: if a guest has a code for a slot, that slot is programmed to that guest.

The household also sets a guest allowance -- how many slots may be programmed at once -- and it
changes that allowance from day to day as visitors come and go. The allowance is only ever reduced
while it is strictly above the number of slots currently programmed, so lowering it never leaves a
programmed slot outside the allowance.

Programming is done by the network's fitters and takes two claims, coarse before fine. A fitter
first takes the hub claim, which only one fitter holds at a time. Holding it, the fitter takes a
claim on an individual slot, and only the fitter holding a slot's claim may touch that slot. It
programs an empty slot to a guest who has no code yet, provided the programmed slots are under the
allowance; it then gives that guest the code for that slot. It can also wipe a slot, which empties
the programming and, at the same moment, cancels the code the guest was given for it, because a
code outstanding on a wiped slot is exactly how two guests end up sharing one slot.

The full set of actions is: a fitter takes the hub claim when it is free; the fitter holding the hub
claim takes a claim on a free slot; the fitter holding a slot's claim programs that empty slot to a
guest with no code, provided the programmed slots are under the allowance; the fitter holding a
slot's claim gives the guest programmed into it the code for that slot; the fitter holding a slot's
claim wipes it, emptying the programming and cancelling that guest's code for it; a fitter gives
back a slot claim; a fitter gives back the hub claim; the household raises the guest allowance; and
the household lowers the guest allowance, only while it is above the slots currently programmed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every guest holding a code for a slot is the guest that slot is currently
programmed to, so a slot is never given out to two guests at once.

---- MODULE W4Od7m4p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Boxes, Grounds, Depth, Free

Booking == [box : Boxes, ground : Grounds]

VARIABLES queue, standing, waiting, armed

vars == <<queue, standing, waiting, armed>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ queue \in Seq(Booking)
    /\ standing \in [Grounds -> Boxes \cup {Free}]
    /\ waiting \subseteq Boxes
    /\ armed \in BOOLEAN

Booked(g) == \E i \in DOMAIN queue : queue[i].ground = g

Init ==
    /\ queue = << >>
    /\ standing = [g \in Grounds |-> Free]
    /\ waiting = Boxes
    /\ armed = FALSE

\* Backpressure: nothing is booked once the queue is at its depth.
Book(b, g) ==
    /\ Len(queue) < Depth
    /\ b \in waiting
    /\ standing[g] = Free
    /\ \A i \in DOMAIN queue : queue[i].ground # g /\ queue[i].box # b
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, [box |-> b, ground |-> g])
    /\ waiting' = waiting \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<standing, armed>>

\* The crane works the front booking; its ground is empty by construction.
Work ==
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![Head(queue).ground] = Head(queue).box]
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, armed>>

LiftOut(g) ==
    /\ standing[g] # Free
    /\ waiting' = waiting \cup {standing[g]}
    /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![g] = Free]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, armed>>

Arm ==
    /\ ~armed
    /\ armed' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, standing, waiting>>

Disarm ==
    /\ armed
    /\ armed' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, standing, waiting>>

\* The override strikes out the bookings its drop would have invalidated.
Drop(b, g) ==
    /\ armed
    /\ b \in waiting
    /\ LET struck == {i \in DOMAIN queue : queue[i].ground = g \/ queue[i].box = b}
           evicted == IF standing[g] = Free THEN {} ELSE {standing[g]}
       IN /\ queue' = SelectSeq(queue, LAMBDA j : j.ground # g /\ j.box # b)
          /\ waiting' = ((waiting \ {b}) \cup evicted)
                          \cup {queue[i].box : i \in struck}
    /\ standing' = [standing EXCEPT ![g] = b]
    /\ UNCHANGED armed

Next ==
    \/ Work \/ Arm \/ Disarm
    \/ \E g \in Grounds : LiftOut(g)
    \/ \E b \in Boxes, g \in Grounds : Book(b, g) \/ Drop(b, g)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(Work)

\* Every queued booking names an empty ground that nothing else has booked.
QueuedGroundsAreFreeAndUnique ==
    \A i \in DOMAIN queue :
        /\ standing[queue[i].ground] = Free
        /\ \A j \in DOMAIN queue : queue[j].ground = queue[i].ground => j = i

\* The queue never stays jammed at its depth.
QueueDrains == (Len(queue) = Depth) ~> (Len(queue) < Depth)

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Boxes = {bxa, bxb, bxc}
    Grounds = {gr1, gr2, gr3}
    Depth = 2
    Free = free

INVARIANT QueuedGroundsAreFreeAndUnique

PROPERTY QueueDrains
nl:
A container-ship crane yard lands containers into numbered ground slots. A slot holds one container,
and the yard planner works through a booking queue: each booking names one waiting container and one
ground slot, and the crane works the queue from the front.

The queue is deliberately short. It has a fixed depth, and when it is full no further booking can
be made until the crane has worked one off the front; this is the yard's backpressure, and it is
what stops the planner from running miles ahead of the crane. A booking can only be made for a
container that is waiting for a slot, for a slot that is standing empty, and for a slot that no
booking already in the queue names; likewise a container already named in the queue cannot be
booked again.

Working the front booking off the queue lands that container into that slot. A container in a slot
can later be lifted out again, which empties the slot and puts the container back among those
waiting.

The yard superintendent holds a privileged override, which can be armed and disarmed. While it is
armed the superintendent can drop a waiting container straight into any slot without going through
the queue at all. Whatever was in that slot is lifted out and goes back to waiting. Because a
booking in the queue for that slot, or for the container just placed, would now be a booking on
something already taken, the override strikes those bookings out of the queue as it goes and puts
their containers back among those waiting.

The full set of actions is: the planner books a waiting container into an empty slot that no queued
booking names, provided the queue is below its depth and the container is not already booked; the
crane works the front booking off the queue, landing that container into that slot; a container is
lifted out of its slot and goes back to waiting; the superintendent arms the override; the
superintendent disarms the override; and the superintendent drops a waiting container straight into
a slot under the armed override, lifting out whatever was there and striking out any queued booking
for that slot or that container.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every booking waiting in the queue names a slot that is still standing empty and
that no other booking in the queue names, so a slot is never booked or landed into twice.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The booking queue never stays full for ever; whenever it is at its depth, it
eventually drops below it again.

EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Readers, Parties, MaxPositions, Free, NoProposal

Positions == 1..MaxPositions

Proposal == [reader : Readers, spot : Positions]

VARIABLES shelf, slip, length, proposal, agreed

vars == <<shelf, slip, length, proposal, agreed>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ shelf \in [Positions -> Readers \cup {Free}]
    /\ slip \in [Readers -> 0..MaxPositions]
    /\ length \in 0..MaxPositions
    /\ proposal \in Proposal \cup {NoProposal}
    /\ agreed \subseteq Parties

Init ==
    /\ shelf = [k \in Positions |-> Free]
    /\ slip = [r \in Readers |-> 0]
    /\ length = 1
    /\ proposal = NoProposal
    /\ agreed = {}

PutUp(r, k) ==
    /\ proposal = NoProposal
    /\ slip[r] = 0
    /\ k <= length
    /\ shelf[k] = Free
    /\ proposal' = [reader |-> r, spot |-> k]
    /\ agreed' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, slip, length>>

Agree(q) ==
    /\ proposal # NoProposal
    /\ q \notin agreed
    /\ agreed' = agreed \cup {q}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, slip, length, proposal>>

\* Everything is re-checked at the moment the reservation goes through.
GoThrough ==
    /\ proposal # NoProposal
    /\ agreed = Parties
    /\ proposal.spot <= length
    /\ shelf[proposal.spot] = Free
    /\ slip[proposal.reader] = 0
    /\ shelf' = [shelf EXCEPT ![proposal.spot] = proposal.reader]
    /\ slip' = [slip EXCEPT ![proposal.reader] = proposal.spot]
    /\ proposal' = NoProposal
    /\ agreed' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED length

Drop ==
    /\ proposal # NoProposal
    /\ proposal' = NoProposal
    /\ agreed' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, slip, length>>

Collect(r) ==
    /\ slip[r] # 0
    /\ shelf' = [shelf EXCEPT ![slip[r]] = Free]
    /\ slip' = [slip EXCEPT ![r] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<length, proposal, agreed>>

AddShelving ==
    /\ length < MaxPositions
    /\ length' = length + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, slip, proposal, agreed>>

\* Shelving only comes off the far end while that position stands empty.
TakeShelving ==
    /\ length > 0
    /\ shelf[length] = Free
    /\ length' = length - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shelf, slip, proposal, agreed>>

Next ==
    \/ GoThrough \/ Drop \/ AddShelving \/ TakeShelving
    \/ \E q \in Parties : Agree(q)
    \/ \E r \in Readers : Collect(r) \/ \E k \in Positions : PutUp(r, k)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A slip always names a live position still holding that reader's book.
SlipsNameLivePositions ==
    \A r \in Readers :
        slip[r] # 0 => (slip[r] <= length /\ shelf[slip[r]] = r)

A library reservation system puts requested books out on a hold shelf. The shelf is a row of
numbered positions, and each position holds the book for one reader. A reader whose reservation has
gone through is given a slip naming the position their book is on.

The shelf's usable length is not fixed. Shelving is added and taken away as the branch reorganises,
so the number of positions actually in use changes during the day. Length is only ever taken away
from the far end, and only while the last position in use is standing empty, so a position with a
book on it is never shelved out from under its reader.

A reservation is not simply written up. The branch and the central catalogue have to agree, so the
branch puts up one proposal at a time, naming a reader who holds no slip and a position that is
within the shelf's current length and standing empty. Each party then records its agreement. The
reservation goes through only when every party has agreed and, at that moment, the position is
still within the length, still standing empty, and the reader still holds no slip; going through
puts the book on that position and hands the reader the slip. A proposal can also be dropped, which
clears the agreements and changes nothing.

When a reader collects, the position is emptied and the slip is spent.

The full set of actions is: the branch puts up a proposal naming a reader with no slip and an empty
position within the shelf's length; a party records its agreement to the proposal; the reservation
goes through once every party has agreed and the position and reader are both still free, putting
the book out and handing over the slip; the proposal is dropped, clearing the agreements; a reader
collects, emptying the position and spending the slip; shelving is added, extending the length; and
shelving is taken away from the far end, only while the last position in use is empty.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every slip a reader holds names a position that is still within the shelf's
current length and still has that reader's book on it, so a position is never given out to two
readers and never left holding a book outside the shelf.
