---- MODULE W4Od13m0p0t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Vans, Free, NoRead

ASSUME Free \notin Vans

VARIABLES register, onPort, reading, brokeDown

vars == <<register, onPort, reading, brokeDown>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ register \in Vans \cup {Free}
    /\ onPort \in [Vans -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ reading \in [Vans -> {"free", "busy", NoRead}]
    /\ brokeDown \subseteq Vans

Running(v) == v \notin brokeDown

Init ==
    /\ register = Free
    /\ onPort = [v \in Vans |-> FALSE]
    /\ reading = [v \in Vans |-> NoRead]
    /\ brokeDown = {}

\* The read reserves nothing; it only records what the register said.
Look(v) ==
    /\ Running(v)
    /\ ~onPort[v]
    /\ reading[v] = NoRead
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![v] = IF register = Free THEN "free" ELSE "busy"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<register, onPort, brokeDown>>

\* The write lands only while the register still reads free.
WriteIn(v) ==
    /\ Running(v)
    /\ reading[v] = "free"
    /\ register = Free
    /\ register' = v
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![v] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onPort, brokeDown>>

Reread(v) ==
    /\ Running(v)
    /\ reading[v] = "busy"
    /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![v] = NoRead]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<register, onPort, brokeDown>>

DriveOn(v) ==
    /\ Running(v)
    /\ register = v
    /\ ~onPort[v]
    /\ onPort' = [onPort EXCEPT ![v] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<register, reading, brokeDown>>

DriveOff(v) ==
    /\ Running(v)
    /\ onPort[v]
    /\ onPort' = [onPort EXCEPT ![v] = FALSE]
    /\ register' = Free
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reading, brokeDown>>

BreakDown(v) ==
    /\ brokeDown = {}
    /\ brokeDown' = {v}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<register, onPort, reading>>

Tow(v) ==
    /\ v \in brokeDown
    /\ onPort[v]
    /\ onPort' = [onPort EXCEPT ![v] = FALSE]
    /\ register' = Free
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reading, brokeDown>>

Stale == register # Free /\ ~onPort[register]

\* A registration nobody drove on against is timed out.
TimeOut ==
    /\ Stale
    /\ register' = Free
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onPort, reading, brokeDown>>

Next ==
    \/ TimeOut
    \/ \E v \in Vans : Look(v) \/ WriteIn(v) \/ Reread(v) \/ DriveOn(v)
                       \/ DriveOff(v) \/ BreakDown(v) \/ Tow(v)

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(TimeOut)

\* Whoever is on the port is the van the register names.
PortMatchesRegister == \A v \in Vans : onPort[v] => register = v

\* A registration is never left standing with nobody on the port.
StaleRegistrationsClear == Stale ~> ~Stale

SPECIFICATION Spec

CONSTANTS
    Vans = {vna, vnb, vnc}
    Free = portfree
    NoRead = noread

INVARIANT PortMatchesRegister

PROPERTY StaleRegistrationsClear
nl:
A vending machine network empties its takings into one depot safe, and the safe has a single
docking port. Only one collection van can be on the port at a time.

The port keeps a register that either reads free or carries a van's name. Vans do not queue and
nothing is reserved for them: a van looks at the register and remembers whether it read free or
busy. A van that read free then tries to write its own name in, and the write only goes through
while the register still reads free; a van that read busy simply throws the reading away and will
look again later. A van whose name is in the register may then drive onto the port, and when it has
finished it drives off, which puts the register back to free.

A van can break down silently at any point. A van that has broken down does nothing further: it
does not look, does not write, does not drive on and does not drive off. The depot's watchdog deals
with the consequences. If a broken-down van is sitting on the port, the watchdog tows it off and
puts the register back to free. Separately, if the register carries a van's name but no van is
actually on the port, the registration has gone stale -- the van that won it may have broken down
before driving on, or simply not come -- and the watchdog times the registration out, putting the
register back to free.

The full set of actions is: a running van that is off the port and holding no reading looks at the
register and remembers free or busy; a running van that read free writes its name in, provided the
register still reads free; a running van that read busy throws the reading away; the van the
register names drives onto the port; a van on the port drives off, putting the register back to
free; a van breaks down; the watchdog tows a broken-down van off the port, putting the register
back to free; and the watchdog times out a registration that no van has driven on against.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any van on the docking port is the van whose name the register currently carries,
so two vans are never on the port together.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A registration is never left standing with nobody on the port; whenever the
register carries a name that no van has driven on against, it is eventually cleared.
